classification.difficultyReason: Connect the sector arc to the cone's base circumference and the sector radius to its slant height, then obtain the perpendicular height using Pythagoras before calculating the exact volume.

content.prompt: The diagram below shows a sector subtended by an angle of $\frac{2\pi}{3}$ from a circle with radius $6$ cm.

spec.description: Sector on the left, transformation arrow in the centre and cone on the right. The sector retains both 6 cm labels, matching single ticks and its interior angle. The cone retains dashed height, radius and rear rim, with a right-angle marker.
spec.mathematics: A sector of radius 6 cm and angle 2pi/3 forms a cone whose slant height is 6 cm. Cone silhouette generators meet the projected base ellipse at calculated tangencies.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown labels h and r are visible.

children.prompt: The straight edges of the sector are joined so that the sector forms a cone. Find the volume of the cone that it forms.

answer.short:
$V=\frac{16\pi\sqrt{2}}{3}\text{ cm}^3$.

The sector arc becomes the base circumference, and the sector radius becomes the slant height.
answer.worked:
The sector arc becomes the circumference of the cone's base.
$$\begin{align*}
l&=6\times\frac{2\pi}{3}\\
l&=4\pi\text{ cm}\\
2\pi r&=4\pi\\
r&=2\text{ cm}.
\end{align*}$$
The slant height is $6$ cm, so Pythagoras gives
$$\begin{align*}
h^2&=6^2-2^2\\
h^2&=32\\
h&=4\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}.
\end{align*}$$
Therefore
$$\begin{align*}
V&=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2h\\
V&=\frac{1}{3}\pi(2)^2(4\sqrt{2})\\
V&=\frac{16\pi\sqrt{2}}{3}\text{ cm}^3.
\end{align*}$$
